references.text: God sends Moses with a mission and gives him signs as proof that he is sent by the Lord.
Moses receives signs from God to prove that the Lord has sent him, addressing the same theme of confirming divine commission.
The criterion for knowing whether a prophet speaks from the Lord or from their own heart – parallel to Moses' statement that he does not act from his own heart.
Continuation of Moses' speech where he describes the sign that will prove the Lord has sent him.
The Lord says He did not send the prophets, yet they ran anyway – in contrast to Moses, who was sent by God.
False prophets speak from their own hearts, not from the mouth of the Lord – Moses emphasizes that he does not speak from his own heart.
God gives signs through His prophets to show that He has sent them.
The prophet says the people will know that the Lord has sent him – using the same wording as Moses.
Zechariah speaks about the people knowing that the Lord has sent him – a parallel to Moses' words.
Jesus points to His works as proof that the Father has sent Him – parallel to Moses pointing to signs as proof of divine commission.
Jesus says His teaching is not His own, but from the One who sent Him – parallel to Moses saying he does not act from his own heart.
